statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of the public age gate and representative support/legal templates. Explicit media content and authenticated account management were not entered; the legal age gate was respected.

page.framework: Server-rendered HTML with jQuery and custom account/modal scripts
page.notes: The root is an age-verification wall in the observed jurisdiction. Representative public templates were audited without bypassing the gate.

Primary age-verification CTA through the resulting account-registration modal, including empty submission.
Long-form policy template representing content-heavy legal pages and long scrolling.
Privacy/2257 policy template, checked for disclosure, localization, mobile layout and consent chrome.

findings.summary: Theme is hard-coded rather than driven by the user’s color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS probe found no color-scheme declaration or prefers-color-scheme rule; dark-emulation output is byte-identical in size to the default capture.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and express surface/text colors with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), preserving a usable light and dark palette.

findings.summary: The age-estimation indicator ignores reduced-motion.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the SVG still contains an indefinite 3-second animate element and no reduced-motion CSS is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable or replace the non-essential looping SVG animation inside a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce query.

findings.summary: The page has no high-contrast or forced-colors adaptation.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no prefers-contrast/forced-colors rules; the increased-contrast screenshot is visually unchanged, while Lighthouse also identifies a 3.83:1 text contrast failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast handling, retain system colors/outlines, and increase low-contrast text colors.

findings.summary: The primary state change is an abrupt custom-overlay swap.
findings.evidence: The interaction video shows the registration surface appearing without a directional or same-document transition; CSS inspection found no view-transition usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a progressively enhanced same-document View Transition for opening/closing the account step, and disable it under reduced motion.

findings.summary: Long policy pages provide no scroll progress or scroll-state-aware chrome.
findings.evidence: The 10,158px-high terms template has static header/chrome; CSS inspection found no scroll-state query, progress indicator, or scroll-driven state.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight progress cue or compact the sticky header based on scroll state, with a non-supporting-browser fallback.

findings.summary: The cookie notice persistently obscures mobile content and offers only dismissal/implied consent.
findings.evidence: Terms, privacy, and FAQ screenshots show a fixed banner covering the bottom lines of content; it says continued use accepts cookies and exposes only “[ X ]”.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, accessible consent surface with clear accept/reject choices, reserve or avoid overlaying reading content, and persist the decision.

findings.summary: The mandatory registration overlay is an ad-hoc modal without dialog semantics.
findings.evidence: The interaction frame shows a modal overlay, but the visible-state probe finds no dialog element or role=dialog; it is built with SimpleModal-style divs.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the custom container with dialog/showModal(), label it, manage initial/return focus, and use native close/cancel behavior.

findings.summary: Mobile support pages devote too much of the viewport to chrome, ads and overlays.
findings.evidence: FAQ begins with header plus a two-tile ad and ends under a cookie overlay; policy screenshots show content hidden behind persistent chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer ads below the help task, reduce fixed chrome, and keep legal/help content unobscured.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is only viewport-wide and lacks component-level adaptation.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container/container-type usage across the reused age-card and content templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries where cards/forms are reused at different widths, retaining existing media queries as fallback where needed.

findings.summary: Footer controls are too small for reliable touch input.
findings.evidence: The focus/geometry probe measured every footer link at 14px high; Lighthouse target-size reports less than the required 24px size/spacing.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase clickable padding/spacing to at least 24x24 CSS px, preferably 44x44 for primary mobile targets, while retaining visible focus.

findings.summary: The “Get You Verified” action unexpectedly dead-ends at mandatory account registration.
findings.evidence: The age wall promises age verification and “no ID required,” but its CTA opens a “Register for free” account form before any age check, an undisclosed detour in the core journey.
findings.suggestedFix: Explain account requirements before activation or, preferably, let users complete age estimation directly and offer account creation separately.

findings.summary: Registration recovery state is incomplete and weakly associated.
findings.evidence: Submitting the empty visible registration form reports only a password-length error, leaves all fields valid with no aria-invalid, and exposes no role=alert/live announcement.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, summarize all actionable errors, associate each message with its field, set aria-invalid, and move/announce focus predictably.

findings.summary: Parser-blocking scripts and CSS delay the small age wall.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identifies two synchronous scripts plus the stylesheet as render-blocking with up to 1,280ms estimated savings; the longest critical chain is 913ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical scripts, avoid loading site-wide behavior before it is needed, and inline or split only the minimal age-wall critical CSS.

findings.summary: The age wall ships mostly unused site-wide CSS and JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 31KiB unused CSS (99.8%) and 35KiB unused JavaScript (84.9%) on this small gate.
findings.suggestedFix: Create an age-wall bundle, conditionally load account/verification code after intent, and remove the old global dependencies from the critical path.

findings.summary: Key images, modal structure and registration fields lack accessible names/relationships.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flags the logo without alt; the registration form uses placeholder-only inputs with no labels, and the visible modal has no dialog role.
findings.suggestedFix: Add appropriate alt text (or empty alt if decorative), explicit labels, dialog name/description, and native semantic controls.

findings.summary: The green age-estimation text fails minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measures #0a910a on #222 at 3.83:1, below the required 4.5:1 for the rendered 19.5px normal-weight text.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose a lighter green or darker background that reaches at least 4.5:1 in every theme and contrast mode.

findings.summary: The age wall lacks a main landmark and H1, and its footer list is malformed.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports no main landmark and a UL containing a direct BR child; the DOM has only an H2 and no landmarks.
findings.suggestedFix: Use main, make the page purpose an H1, keep only LI children in UL, and verify modal focus trapping and return.

findings.summary: Long legal text is cramped and partially obscured on mobile.
findings.evidence: The terms screenshot shows dense 12.5px copy in a narrow column while the fixed cookie bar covers the current lines.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase body size/line-height, constrain readable measure, add section spacing, and ensure overlays do not cover text.

findings.summary: Touch-target accessibility fails despite successful viewport reflow.
findings.evidence: The 360px layouts do not overflow, but Lighthouse identifies multiple 14px-high footer targets with insufficient spacing.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve the good reflow while increasing interactive target dimensions and spacing across zoomed/narrow layouts.

findings.summary: Images lack intrinsic dimensions and some content images lack alternatives.
findings.evidence: The entry image audit finds both images unsized; the FAQ audit finds all 23 images unsized and six missing alt values.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width/height or aspect-ratio and meaningful/empty alt values as appropriate; keep dimensions consistent with responsive CSS.

findings.summary: The public age-verification entry has no meta description.
findings.evidence: DOM and Lighthouse show a title but no meta[name=description], producing an SEO audit failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise, localized description that accurately explains the legal age-verification gate.

findings.summary: The entry lacks canonical/localization signals and unknown URLs return false-success pages.
findings.evidence: The home probe finds no canonical or hreflang; an intentionally nonexistent URL returns HTTP 200 with the age wall.
findings.suggestedFix: Return real 404 status/content for unknown routes and add canonical plus localized hreflang links to public entry pages.

findings.summary: The public entry exposes no share-preview or structured metadata.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found no Open Graph title/description/image and no JSON-LD.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate localized Open Graph metadata and Organization/WebSite JSON-LD where it reflects visible content.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but CSP and cookie protections are insufficient.
findings.evidence: CSP only upgrades insecure requests; epcolor lacks Secure and uses SameSite=None, while EPRNS also uses SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive nonce/hash-based CSP and set Secure plus Lax/Strict SameSite on cookies unless cross-site use is demonstrably required.

findings.summary: Account authentication offers federated/password paths but no phishing-resistant passkey path.
findings.evidence: The registration modal exposes social/password account options; source/probes show no WebAuthn/passkey affordance. Camera permission is at least deferred to an explicit button.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey registration and authentication alongside existing options, with conditional UI where supported.

findings.summary: Defensive response policies are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Header inspection finds no X-Content-Type-Options or Referrer-Policy; Permissions-Policy grants broad client-hint access and CSP lacks frame-ancestors/Trusted Types restrictions.
findings.suggestedFix: Add nosniff, a strict Referrer-Policy, least-privilege Permissions-Policy and CSP frame-ancestors; evaluate Trusted Types for the script-heavy account UI.

findings.summary: Unknown routes fail silently as a successful age-wall response.
findings.evidence: The intentional nonexistent route returned HTTP 200 and the normal age-verification HTML instead of a 404/recovery page.
findings.suggestedFix: Return correct error status codes and a localized recovery page with useful navigation; apply equivalent intentional states to fetch/network failures.

findings.summary: Critical content is English on the Spanish host, and the entry has no language declaration.
findings.evidence: The age wall and legal documents are English at es.eporner.com; the entry html lang is empty, while terms declares es despite English headings/body.
findings.suggestedFix: Translate the complete gate and policy templates, set accurate per-page lang, and use logical properties so localized layouts remain robust.

findings.summary: The age CTA conceals an account-creation requirement, and cookie consent is implied.
findings.evidence: “Let’s Get You Verified” unexpectedly opens registration; support pages say continued use accepts cookies and offer only an X, with no reject choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate age verification from account acquisition, disclose every prerequisite before the CTA, and provide symmetric consent choices without implied acceptance.

findings.summary: Registration validation is neither field-complete nor accessibly announced.
findings.evidence: Empty submit reports only a password-length message, uses no required attributes/aria-invalid, and does not expose the error as a live alert.
findings.suggestedFix: Use required/type=email constraints plus post-interaction validation, field-specific messages, error summary, aria-describedby and live announcement.

findings.summary: The signup form actively disables useful autofill.
findings.evidence: Login, password, confirmation and email fields all use autocomplete=off; none provide username, new-password or email tokens.
findings.suggestedFix: Use username, new-password and email autocomplete tokens and appropriate input types so password managers and browser autofill can assist.

findings.summary: The account flow is disproportionate to the requested age check and lacks a modern, clearly reversible path.
findings.evidence: The gate forces registration before verification; the visible modal offers password/social registration but no passkey and no clearly labelled cancel action in the captured surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Make account creation optional, add an explicit cancel/back action with focus return, and support passkeys for users who choose an account.

findings.summary: Image delivery misses basic dimension and format efficiencies.
findings.evidence: The FAQ image audit finds 23 unsized images, seven legacy-format assets and no responsive source data for content thumbnails; the entry uses an unsized GIF.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive AVIF/WebP sources where appropriate, include intrinsic dimensions, and avoid legacy GIF/JPEG when a lighter format preserves the content.

taskList.title: Make age verification direct, transparent and optional-account
Rebuild modal and registration semantics, validation and autofill
Fully localize the Spanish gate and policy templates
Fix visual accessibility, target sizes and reading comfort
Harden CSP, browser policies and cookie attributes
Honor color, motion and contrast preferences
Split and defer the age-wall CSS/JavaScript payload
Correct entry metadata, canonicalization and 404 behavior
Remove obstructive chrome and implement honest cookie consent
Add intrinsic dimensions and modern responsive image delivery
Add proportionate modern responsive and transition cues
Offer passkey authentication for users choosing an account

checkOutcomes.method: compare heap snapshots for retained growth - a baseline, then one taken after repeating the interaction with `--interact` about 10x (the memory-tracer methodology: baseline -> repeat -> post -> compare). Performance.getMetrics (JSHeapUsedSize, Nodes) across the same before/after window is corroboration. If Chrome DevTools MCP is available, follow its memory-leak-debugging skill: capture baseline, target, and final snapshots, then use memlab or the provided comparison workflow rather than reading
checkOutcomes.evidence: After one modal interaction the heap was 33,552,152 bytes/141,325 nodes; after ten attempts it was 33,798,066 bytes/143,707 nodes, only 0.7%/1.7% higher rather than repeated one-time growth.

checkOutcomes.method: a single `heap` summary's totals (nodeCount, totalSelfSizeBytes, constructor population) plus Performance.getMetrics (Nodes, JSHeapUsedSize) give the current footprint to judge against the page's purpose. Chrome DevTools MCP heap snapshots and memlab snapshot analysis can provide the same memory distribution when available. Read summaries or derived analysis, never raw snapshots unless a dedicated heap-analysis tool is doing the analysis. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Baseline is 4.2MB; after loading the account and on-device age-model UI once, the retained heap plateaus near 33.8MB, proportionate to that feature.
